Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated ramp plan, GPU profile & VPC decision

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we stay aligned: 

- CedarStreet preference: leaning Dedicated capacity with VPC (private network) for PHI and audit controls, but still evaluating cost tradeoffs vs Hosted API for non-sensitive traffic.
- Clarify numbers we need to finalize a sizing recommendation:
  * Peak TPS target (open question on burst vs steady)
  * Concurrent active requests desired (slot/concurrency target)
  * Typical token mix (avg tokens per request + % long-form)
  * Latency SLO (p50/p95 targets) and any regional constraints

I've attached a quick compute estimate worksheet and our SKU guide — will use your answers below to produce a short dedicated configuration (GPU type, slots, estimated monthly spend).

Action items for CedarStreet: please confirm the bullets below so we can lock a PoC config:
- Peak sustained TPS and estimated burst factor (e.g., 120 TPS sustained, 2x burst)
- Average tokens per request and % of requests >1000 tokens
- Whether both interactive and batch workloads will share the same pool
- Any compliance/procurement timelines (rough dates)

Thanks — I looped Marissa to help with the sizing and Karthik for kernel/quantization guidance on our side.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@cedarstreet.com>

Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated ramp plan, GPU profile & VPC decision

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the summary. Answers below: 

- Deployment: We want Dedicated + VPC for production (PHI). We may keep some non-PHI endpoints on Hosted for cost reasons, but prod must be private.
- Traffic profile:
  * Peak sustained TPS: 100–140 TPS (planning for 120 TPS baseline)
  * Burst: short bursts up to ~2.5x sustained for 5–10 minutes during morning syncs
  * Concurrent active requests: roughly 6–10 concurrent live sessions during peak (concurrent inference operations, not client connections)
  * Token mix: avg ~320 tokens/request; ~92% under 600 tokens; ~8% long-form (1k–1.5k tokens) — long requests are critical for nightly summaries
  * Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for standard prompts; p95 <= 2s tolerated for long-form.
- Workloads: interactive inference for end-user assistants plus scheduled nightly batch summarization jobs that can be routed to a separate tenant/pool if needed.
- Compliance/procurement: we aim to have procurement signoff by Nov 15; technical PoC in the next 3 weeks would be ideal.

Q: What GPU do you recommend for the mix — H100 for latency or A100 for cost? Also curious how prefix caching might reduce slot count for the nightly summaries.

Laura
Head of ML Platforms | CedarStreet Health

I'm planning to circle back to Laura with a 1-page recommended configuration and a PoC proposal today.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated ramp plan, GPU profile & VPC decision

Thanks — great detail from the CedarStreet team. Quick recommendation draft for Rishi to send as a follow-up (high level + numbers):

1) Recommended baseline dedicated configuration (PoC-focused):
   - GPUs: start with 4 x H100 (or 2 H100 + 2 A100 mixed if cost pressure is high). H100 gives headroom for p95 latency; mixed pool can reduce burn.
   - Slots/instances: configure 32 concurrency slots across the pool (roughly 8 slots per H100). This assumes average token length ~320 and batching turned on for short prompts. Slots map to active model contexts; adjust after PoC.
   - Burst strategy: enable autoscale with buffer capacity to cover 2.5x short bursts; target cold-start warm pool of 1 GPU for fast scaling.
   - Long-form handling: route long requests to a separate slot queue (or a lower-priority pool) to avoid blocking short interactive latency. Alternatively schedule nightly batch to a separate tenant/pool for best cost-efficiency.

2) Expected throughput math (estimate):
   - With 4 H100 and 32 slots, optimistic sustained throughput ~100–140 TPS for short prompts with batching; long-form concurrently will reduce short-prompt throughput — that's why we isolate long jobs.
   - Prefix/KV caching: for repeated context (nightly summaries with consistent prefixes), caching can cut CPU/GPU work for prefixes and effectively increase effective throughput for short prompts — recommend enabling KV cache for the PoC and measuring slot utilization over the first 72 hours.

3) Security & VPC notes:
   - VPC private control plane + customer-managed KMS recommended for PHI. Provide SOC2 evidence and audit log export to your security team during the PoC.

4) Next steps & timeline:
   - Rishi: send this recommendation to Laura + attach updated compute worksheet and PoC scope (I can prepare the PoC playbook).
   - Proposed PoC: 3-week PoC starting as early as Oct 11 — baseline telemetry collection (latency, slot utilization, token distribution), then a tuning week.
   - Procurement: Marissa will provide a rough procurement checklist and pricing delta for mixed vs H100-only pools. Procurement contact cc'd.

Attachments to include in reply: cedarstreet_compute_estimate_v2.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-sku-guide.pdf

If agreed, we can schedule a technical deep dive next week with our runtime team to confirm batching/quantization knobs and exact slot definitions.

Marissa
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
